links.comparator_used: Plaintext federated learning (unencrypted model updates), also compared with centralised learning and differential-privacy baselines
links.outcome: Membership-inference attack AUC (privacy) versus predictive utility (F1, ROC-AUC) and communication cost
links.effect: HE-FL reduced membership-inference AUC to 0.5000 (random guess); plaintext FL had F1 = 0.9922 and ROC-AUC = 0.9996 versus HE-FL F1 = 0.4042 and ROC-AUC = 0.7714; uplink rose from 3.18 MB to 37.69 MB per round (~24× ciphertext expansion)
links.tradeoff: Large utility loss, convergence degradation, approximately 24× ciphertext expansion, and uplink increase from 3.18 MB to 37.69 MB per round
links.quote: Plaintext FL achieved the highest utility (F1 = 0.9922; ROC-AUC = 0.9996), whereas the proposed HE-FL configuration retained meaningful predictive capability (F1 = 0.4042; ROC-AUC = 0.7714) and reduced membership-inference attack performance to the random-guess level (AUC = 0.5000) under the evaluated protocol.

links.comparator_used: Centralised learning on pooled data from the same simulated hospitals
links.outcome: Predictive performance and privacy of federated versus centralised training
links.effect: The abstract reports plaintext FL utility (F1 = 0.9922; ROC-AUC = 0.9996) but gives no centralised numbers or direct comparison result.
links.quote: The framework is compared with centralised learning, plaintext FL, and differential-privacy baselines using predictive, privacy, and systems metrics.

design_hint: homomorphic encryption of federated learning updates
